title: Late Charge Assessment on an Overdue Home Mortgage Loans Installment
content:
**Clause 1.** A late charge applies to an installment on a Home Mortgage Loans note that has not been received in full within the program's grace period, counted in calendar days after that installment's due date.

**Clause 2.** Calendar days are counted with the day after the installment's due date as day 1. The charge applies when the installment is still unpaid after the end of the last grace day.

**Clause 3.** The charge equals the program's late charge rate for the borrower's state of residence, taken as a percent of the principal and interest part of the installment, rounded half-up to the cent. Escrow is never part of the basis.

**Clause 4.** Each installment carries at most one late charge.

**Clause 5.** No late charge applies during forbearance.

## Both sides of the grace period

Take a hypothetical installment on a program whose grace period is 15 calendar days, still unpaid.

- Counted with the day after its due date as day 1, the fifteenth such day is the last grace day. On that fifteenth day the grace period has not yet ended, so no charge applies.
- On the sixteenth day after the due date the last grace day has ended and the installment is still unpaid, so the charge applies.

## Worked figure on hypothetical inputs

Take an installment whose principal and interest part is $1500.00 and whose escrow part is $300.00, on a loan whose borrower resides in South Carolina, on a program whose rate for that state is 5.00 percent. The basis is the principal and interest part alone, so five hundredths of $1500.00 gives a late charge of $75.00, which falls on the cent.

Had the same borrower resided in North Carolina, on a program whose rate for that state is 4.00 percent, four hundredths of $1500.00 would give $60.00.

## Points of judgement

An installment already carrying a late charge takes no second one, however long it stays unpaid. While the loan stands in forbearance, no late charge is assessed on it at all.
